system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**CONFIDENTIAL – PRIVILEGED – BUYER EYES ONLY**  
**Project Kestrel – Seller Mark-up vs. Playbook: Critical Departures & Push-back Plan**  

---

### 1. LIABILITY REGIME – FUNDAMENTAL RE-ARCHITECTURE REQUIRED  

| Playbook Baseline | Seller Position | Assessment |
|-------------------|----------------|------------|
| **Cap**: 25% / AUD 6 M (20% / 4.8 M *only* with Amelia Frost written authority – **none given**) | 20% / AUD 4.8 M (Cl. 12.1) | **Hard departure.** Seller treats the fallback as the starting point. We must hold 25% / 6 M. |
| **De minimis**: AUD 5 k; **Basket**: AUD 50 k (first-dollar recovery once exceeded) | De minimis AUD 25 k; Basket AUD 250 k (excess-only) (Cl. 12.2) | **Hard departure.** Seller’s thresholds are 5×/5× ours and shift risk via excess-only basket. |
| **General claims period**: 24 months (18 months *only* with Amelia Frost written approval – **none given**) | 18 months (Cl. 12.3/13) | **Hard departure.** Seller proposes the fallback without authority. |
| **Fundamental/Title**: Separate regime – 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Capacity & title warranties subject to *same* caps, time limits, baskets as general warranties (Cl. 12.1/12.3) | **Hard departure.** This collapses the fundamental regime into the general regime – unacceptable. |
| **Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct**: Carved out of **all** caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, non-reliance – non-waivable | Limitations, exclusive-remedy & non-reliance provisions apply to **all Claims of any nature** (Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5) | **Hard departure.** Seller expressly sweeps fraud into the general regime. This is a non-starter. |
| **“Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise”** (Cl. 13) | | **Drafting trap** – would override any separate fundamental/fraud carve-outs unless we insert explicit “notwithstanding” language. |

**Push-back**:  
- Cap at 25% / AUD 6 M.  
- De minimis AUD 5 k; basket AUD 50 k (first-dollar).  
- General claims period 24 months.  
- Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, tax, IP) – 100% cap, 6+ years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.  
- Fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct: express carve-out from *every* limitation, exclusive remedy, non-reliance clause.  
- Delete “limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise”; replace with “nothing in this Agreement limits liability for Fraud, Fundamental Warranties, Tax, IP or Specific Indemnities.”

---

### 2. DISCLOSURE & BUYER KNOWLEDGE – REJECT BLANKET DEEMED KNOWLEDGE  

| Playbook | Seller Position | Assessment |
|----------|----------------|------------|
| **Specific fair disclosure only**; reject whole-data-room, public-register, prudent-search deemed disclosure | General disclosure of *entire* data room (DD-002 to DD-012) + statutory registers + public registers (Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]) | **Hard departure.** “Everything in the data room” is not fair disclosure. |
| **Buyer knowledge**: No blanket exclusion; any qualifier requires *named Seller knowledge persons* + reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnity | “Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records” (Cl. 8.3) | **Hard departure.** Blanket constructive-knowledge bar tied to data-room trawl; would defeat specific indemnities and fundamental warranties. |

**Push-back**:  
- Disclosure Letter: only *specific*, *identified* matters (schedule of material contracts, litigation, IP, etc.). Delete general data-room/public-register disclosure.  
- Cl. 8.3: Delete entirely. If Seller insists on a knowledge qualifier, limit to *actual* knowledge of *named* Buyer signatories (not advisers) and carve out title, capacity, fraud, tax, IP, specific indemnities.  
- Add “fair disclosure” standard: matter must be disclosed in sufficient detail to enable Buyer to assess its impact.

---

### 3. CONDITIONS PRECEDENT – BLUEFEN & RIVERLARK: NO POST-COMPLETION RISK  

#### Bluefen (Material Customer – ~30% revenue)  
| Playbook | Seller Position | Assessment |
|----------|----------------|------------|
| Effective consent **AND evidence conditions satisfied** *before* Completion; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on *delivery of written consent* (Cl. 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter [2]: **no final written consent, no evidence conditions satisfied** | **Hard departure.** Seller wants to close without confirmed consent or condition satisfaction. “Reasonable endeavours” + “consent-on-delivery” = Buyer bears revocation/condition-failure risk. |

#### Riverlark (AUD ~3.2 M debt)  
| Playbook | Seller Position | Assessment |
|----------|----------------|------------|
| Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases *at* Completion; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval | Release to be provided *following* Completion (Cl. 2/7). Disclosure Letter [3]: **facility not repaid, no final discharge** | **Hard departure.** Seller proposes post-Completion discharge with no irrevocable undertaking, no buyer approval. Buyer would own a target encumbered by AUD 3.2 M secured debt. |

**Push-back**:  
- **Bluefen**: Condition Precedent = written consent *plus* certified copy of consent showing all Cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied/waived. No “reasonable endeavours” qualifier.  
- **Riverlark**: Mandatory repayment from Completion funds (funds flow line item); security releases delivered *at* Completion. If Seller insists on post-Completion release: irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark + Amelia Frost written sign-off.  
- Both: “No Completion until satisfied” – not “reasonable endeavours.”

---

### 4. SPECIFIC COMMERCIAL ITEMS – FUNDS FLOW & INDEMNITIES  

| Item | Playbook | Seller Position / Disclosure | Gap / Risk |
|------|----------|------------------------------|------------|
| **Employee bonuses (DD-005)** | AUD 420 k + triggered on-costs = specific line item or Seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude | Bonuses “matter for Seller, not separately itemised in funds flow” (Funds flow note). Disclosure [5]: **on-costs (payroll tax, super) not stated** | **Silent exclusion.** Buyer would inherit AUD 420 k + ~AUD 80–100 k on-costs post-Completion. |
| **Ironquay IP (DD-004/DD-010)** | Broaden narrow indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180 k not independently verified | Existing indemnity limited to SOW3 payment “considered adequate” (Cl. 11.1). Disclosure [4]: **no receipt of payment, no confirmatory assignment** | **Narrow indemnity + unverified payment.** If fees unpaid, IP transfer fails – Buyer gets no cure. |
| **Export/privacy incident (DD-006)** | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; **assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand** | “Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material” (Cl. 4.6). Disclosure [6]: **investigation preliminary; no confirmed breach, scope, or notification duty** | **Alignment on “no confirmed breach” but Seller prematurely concludes “not material.”** Need contractual investigation covenant + specific indemnity if notification/loss arises. |
| **Sandbar renewals (AUD 330 k)** | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | “Ordinary-course operating costs” (Supplier renewals note). Disclosure [8]: **does not state if unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course** | **Assessment needed.** Not a price-deduction item per playbook, but require representation they are ordinary-course & terminable
=== END ADVICE ===
